title: What Causes Flight Delays?
text:
In 2013, 336,776 flights departed from New York City’s three major airports: JFK, LaGuardia (LGA), and Newark (EWR). This page looks at when departures were scheduled and how late they left.
The word causes is a big question: these records can reveal patterns and associations, but they cannot by themselves prove why a particular flight was delayed. Weather, congestion, and airline operations are possible factors, but we would need additional data to test their effects.

title: What Causes Flight Delays?
text:
Departure time and delay
Each dot below represents one flight with a recorded departure delay. The horizontal axis is its scheduled departure time; the vertical axis is how many minutes early or late it actually departed. The view is zoomed to delays between 30 minutes early and 3 hours late so the dense cluster is easier to see.


Code
flights |>
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) |>
  mutate(
    scheduled_hour = sched_dep_time %/% 100 +
      (sched_dep_time %% 100) / 60
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = scheduled_hour, y = dep_delay)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.08, size = 0.35, color = "#176B87") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 3),
    limits = c(0, 24),
    labels = \(x) sprintf("%02d:00", x)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-30, 180)) +
  labs(
    x = "Scheduled departure time",
    y = "Departure delay (minutes)",
    caption = "Flights with missing departure-delay values are omitted."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)








Figure 1: Each point is a flight; the y-axis is zoomed to show the main cluster.





The points are heavily concentrated near zero delay, with a thinner spread of long delays. Later scheduled flights often appear higher in the plot, but this pattern is descriptive—not proof that the time of day itself causes delays.

title: What Causes Flight Delays?
section: Thousands of flights, grouped by delay
text:
Thousands of flights, grouped by delay
This histogram summarizes the same flight records in bins. The bar heights show how many flights fell into each delay range, and the dashed line marks a 15-minute delay.


Code
flights |>
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dep_delay)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "#176B87", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 15,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#C4492D",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-30, 180)) +
  labs(
    x = "Departure delay (minutes; early departures are negative)",
    y = "Number of flights",
    caption = "The x-axis is zoomed to −30 to 180 minutes; the dashed line is 15 minutes late."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)








Figure 2: Departure-delay counts for 328,521 flights with recorded values.





Of the 328,521 flights with recorded departure delays, 200,089 left on time or early, and 70,774 left more than 15 minutes late. The remaining flights were delayed by 15 minutes or less. This is a useful description of departures, but it does not identify which factors produced the delays.

title: What Causes Flight Delays?
text:
About the data
The data come from the nycflights13 R package. Each row represents a scheduled flight. Missing departure delays generally correspond to flights that did not depart, so the charts describe flights with an observed departure—not cancellations.
